subject: Sessions write into the tree the owner commits from
recordedOccasion: on the owner's observation that a session should hold its changes until told to release them.
severity: two findings are high. Both are silent — nothing fails, and the damage is to what the record can be trusted to mean.
scope: cross-cutting. Tracked files only; the artifact volume is out of scope and finding F6 says why.
read: `git status` and `git log` across the two concurrent sessions
all 27 existing findings bundles, checked for overlap

members.statement: Two sessions' uncommitted work interleaves in shared files, so neither can be committed alone
members.sectionHeading: F1 — two sessions' work interleaves in files neither owns alone

resolution.whatWasDone: §0 gains the rebase step and `git --no-optional-locks` for every git read of the checkout

members.statement: A revision's claimed validator baselines are measured on a tree containing another session's work
members.sectionHeading: F2 — a revision's validation is measured on somebody else's tree

resolution.whatWasDone: Nothing here. §0 step 2 and `docs/rules/README.md` §6's never-quote-`OK` rule

members.statement: A session's work has no diff boundary, so the owner cannot review it as a unit
members.sectionHeading: F3 — no diff boundary, so no unit to review

members.statement: Backing out one session's change is surgical, because `git checkout` would take the other's too

resolution.whatWasDone: §0 step 5 states the asymmetry it always relied on: declining a patch is free, reverting after an apply is not

members.statement: A session can amend a revision the owner has already committed
members.sectionHeading: F5 — a session can amend what the owner has already committed

resolution.whatWasDone: Nothing here. §7 takes the number at apply time; the helper's path is corrected in `resolutions.md`

members.statement: The write discipline does not distinguish the write kinds `docs/legend.md` now names
members.sectionHeading: F6 — the write kinds are named but the discipline is not

resolution.whatWasDone: Nothing here. §6 carries four write kinds with composition stated once; the relocation from `docs/legend.md` is recorded

members.statement: A rule here is enforceable at write time only where the fact is in `metadata.json`, the actor identifies itself, and a false refusal costs less than the rule — and none of the four guards that pass those tests is built
members.sectionHeading: F7 — the write discipline has no instrument, and four are available

resolution.whatWasDone: Nothing built. §3 of `rule-enforcement-avenues.md` gains test 3.0 and §4 re-scores all four candidates against it; the avenue available is the checker

members.statement: The guard D7 chose cannot fire at the moment that has actually failed: every recorded instance is the owner committing, and no session-side hook observes that
members.sectionHeading: F8 — the first guard cannot guard the half that has failed

resolution.whatWasDone: §4.1 carries its route — the committing is the owner's and reaches no hook. Built as a checker at Revision 278 instead

members.statement: Two of the three hooks are annotators that cannot refuse anything, and both are scoped to the one directory a session must never write in — so they can only speak about a write the third hook refuses
members.sectionHeading: F9 — the two annotators can only speak about a write that does not happen

resolution.whatWasDone: §3.0's third route, with Revision 282's measurement; the installed set is corrected to one guard and two annotators

members.statement: §0 step 1 places no condition on the checkout it copies and keeps no record of its state, so a patch composed from a dirty copy silently includes another session's work and step 2's promise about the numbers is inverted
members.sectionHeading: F10 — the copy is taken without a condition and without a record

resolution.whatWasDone: §0 step 1 records `git status --porcelain` at copy time, step 3 compares the patch's file list against it, and step 2's promise is qualified to the clean case

members.statement: §0's patch recipe drops a deletion: `git add -N .` stages a removal, and bare `git diff` then compares the working tree against the index and reports nothing, so the patch omits the file silently and `git apply` exits 0
members.sectionHeading: F11 — the patch recipe drops a deletion, silently

resolution.whatWasDone: §0 step 3's recipe is `git diff HEAD`, with the reason recorded in the step; the two forms are byte-identical wherever no deletion is present

members.statement: `verify-doc-paths.sh --all` reads untracked files, so it returns a different verdict in the owner's checkout than in the scratch clone §0 step 2 requires every verification to be run in
members.sectionHeading: F12 — an instrument answers differently in the checkout and in the clone

resolution.whatWasDone: Nothing written. `0012` D2 was accepted 2026-09-04 and carried out by the owner at Revision 310: `.internal/restore/` removed locally, which D2 states is not a repository change. The checkout and a clone now both read `MISSING: 24`, where they read 10 against 20

decisions.decision: The shared-tree collision is not prevented and is not meant to be: it moves to the patch, where it is visible. §0 gains the rebase step, and `git --no-optional-locks` for every git read of the checkout
decisions.sectionHeading: D1 — the collision is not prevented, it is made visible

decisions.decision: F2 is answered by §0 step 2 and by the standing rule never to quote an `OK` total; the enforcement half is F7's and is not folded in here
decisions.sectionHeading: D2 — the baseline question is answered; the enforcement question is F7's

decisions.decision: F3 is answered by §0 steps 3–4 and `bin/review-changes.sh`, both installed at Revision 232
decisions.sectionHeading: D3 — the diff boundary exists and has been used

decisions.decision: F4's remedy holds and has never been stated: declining a patch is free and reverting a commit is not. §0 step 5 now says so
decisions.sectionHeading: D4 — the cheapest thing in the cycle was never written down

decisions.decision: F5 is answered by §7; the artifact `0028` named is at a different path and the citation is corrected rather than the tool moved back
decisions.sectionHeading: D5 — the rule holds and the artifact moved

decisions.decision: F6 is answered by §6's four write kinds; the legend section `0028` created for it no longer exists, the rule having moved to the instruction set, and the relocation is recorded rather than reversed
decisions.sectionHeading: D6 — the rule survived; the section it lived in did not

decisions.decision: Of the four guards F7 names, the manifest-entry guard is built first, warn-only until a clean pass. Nothing is built in this revision and F7 stays `decided`
decisions.sectionHeading: D7 — the order is decided and nothing is built

decisions.decision: A fourth test goes into `docs/rules/rule-enforcement-avenues.md` §3, first, and it asks whether the instrument can observe the act at all. All four candidates in §4 are re-scored against it and all four fail, by three routes. The installed set is corrected: one guard, two annotators
decisions.sectionHeading: D8 — the test that disqualifies before the other three are worth applying

decisions.decision: Record the dirt rather than require a clean copy: `git status --porcelain` captured at §0 step 1, compared against the patch's file list at step 3, and step 2's promise qualified to the clean case
decisions.sectionHeading: D9 — record the dirt, because requiring a clean copy costs more than it saves

decisions.decision: §0 step 3's recipe becomes `git diff HEAD`, the two forms being byte-identical wherever no deletion is present, so the correct one is never worse
decisions.sectionHeading: D10 — `git diff HEAD`, because the short form is never better

decisions.decision: `0012` D2 is adopted as F12's answer rather than cited as it: the empty directory is removed locally, that is not a repository change, and it was carried out at Revision 310
decisions.sectionHeading: D11 — adopt the other bundle's decision, do not borrow it

edges.why: 0049 is 0038's rule broken by a session that had read it; the reading and the recurrence belong together
